images.title: Three bins for a claim
images.purpose: Recap the sorting routine: read the cells a statement compares, then drop it into justified, not justified or cannot tell.
images.composition: A small grid at the top left with one highlighted pair of cells, a statement card with an arrow, and three bins along the bottom; lots of white space.
exact_structure: Top left: a small table of 3 rows by 3 columns with no numbers, two of its cells filled reddish purple (#CC79A7).
A magnifying glass outline in grey (#6B7280) over the two purple cells.
Centre: one blank rounded card labelled statement, with a grey arrow pointing down towards the bins.

Bottom: exactly 3 open bins side by side: green (#009E73) with a tick labelled Justified, vermilion (#D55E00) with a cross labelled Not justified, grey (#6B7280) with a question mark labelled Cannot tell.
rejection: numbers or words written in the table
images.takeaway: Every claim goes to one of three bins, decided by the exact cells it compares.
images.description: A blank table with two highlighted cells, a statement card, and three bins labelled Justified, Not justified and Cannot tell.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Remind students to point to the two cells before choosing a bin.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap visual of the three way sorting routine.
